items.title: BIG’s hanna johansson on designing ‘park rise’ as a vertical extension of athens’ landscape
items.summary_original: BIG’s Hanna Johansson on the future for housing in Athens Set within the vast transformation of Athens’ former international airport, Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG)’s Park Rise is conceived as a residential landmark for The Ellinikon (find designboom's previous coverage here ). The 50-meter tower will anchor Little Athens, a residential neighborhood within the larger coastal masterplan , bringing 88 homes together with gardens, communal amenities, and expansive views across the Aegean Sea, the Metropolitan Park, and the mountains of Attica. For BIG, the project presented an opportunity to work simultaneously across multiple scales. In conversation with designboom, Hanna Johansson, Associate in Charge at BIG, reflects on the studio’s approach to the project and its ambitions for housing in Athen

items.title: first single-family home in greece achieves LEED platinum certification for sustainable living
items.summary_original: HOME UNIFIES ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING AND SMART SYSTEMS Greek studio ECLÉDE designs a 425-square-meter residence located between Lycabettus Hill and Kolonaki. Named Boomerang Athens, this is the first single-family home in Greece to achieve LEED Platinum certification under LEED v4.1 BD+C, the world's most widely recognized green building rating system, providing a global framework for healthy, efficient, and cost-effective architecture. Designed as a climate-responsive urban home, the project unifies architecture, engineering, smart automation , and material restraint into a cohesive concept. Central to its environmental design, a rhythmic vertical screen controls solar exposure and privacy while filtering shifting shadow patterns indoors. Integrated planting zones weave greenery across

items.summary_original: The Bogota-based artist explains how a collection of hand-pinched ceramics, made in the days after an earthquake hit her home country, became a meditation on what keeps the world habitable. Danna Gutiérrez is a visual artist from Cali, Colombia, now based in Bogota, working under the name Gallina Clueka – an experimental multidisciplinary project that treats drawing as a starting point rather than a destination with an end point. What begins as an image on paper regularly ends up in a different form as a ceramic vessel, a piece of jewellery, a print or a textile. items.summary_original: Die KI-Kennzeichnungspflicht ist jetzt da – und der GWA hat dazu eine Umfrage gestartet. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass Agenturen mehr Beratungsleistung schaffen müssen und dass sich auf Consumer-Seite momentan noch ein ungenaues Bild abzeichnet. Die KI-Kennzeichnungspflicht ist offiziell Realität. Doch welchen Einfluss hat die neue Regulierung auf die Werbebranche? Eine aktuelle Umfrage des Gesamtverbands Kommunikationsagenturen (GWA), die zwischen dem 31. Juli und dem 31. August 2026 unter den Mitgliedsagenturen durchgeführt wurde, liefert Antworten. Die Grundstimmung ist erstmal positiv: Rund 66 Prozent der befragten Agenturen begrüßen die neue Kennzeichnungspflicht. items.title: Poster Safari Zurich 2026
items.summary_original: This year, Poster Safari returns for its fourth edition in Zurich's District 5. In a place where commercial messages usually dominate the urban landscape, 20 designers take over large-scale advertising billboards, transforming them with their own interpretations of this year's theme, OUT OF…, into animated visual statements. By scanning the posters with the smartphone, visitors can experience them in augmented reality and discover an additional dimension of design. With works by: allink, Andrés Acosta, Blaschitz, bergerberg, Büro Haeberli, Elizaveta Skargina, Eunbee Lee × Dongjun Choi, Fabian Luginbühl × Emma Leuthold, JEFF Zürich, mdbuero, Modo, Pia Fleischmann, Sandro Staudenmann, Simon Haerter, Stojan, Studio Chouchou, Studio Flux, Studio Heyday, Superdot, Upset, WePlayDesign Jury: Eric

items.summary_original: A PURPLE TEXTILE REFLECTS SUNLIGHT AND RELEASES HEAT A new purple cooling fabric developed by researchers at Zhengzhou University in China and the University of Adelaide in Australia challenges the idea that the coolest option must be white. In Thomke Meyer's illustrations, you'll spot hair whipping sideways, vines coiling and unravelling across a page, figures leaning mid-stride as if the wind is about to set them afloat. items.summary_original: The award-winning studio has spent years proving creativity doesn't need a postcode. So why are they now heading for the Big Smoke? Even in 2026, some people get sniffy about the idea of running a design studio outside of London. Especially somewhere like Falmouth, 300 miles away on the west coast of England. And yet that's exactly where Studio Kiln decided to set up shop, back in 2022. And since then, it's all gone surprisingly well. The creative practice has won a number of awards and built a strong reputation for its branding and digital work, such as its particle system for BAFTA . It's all powerful proof that you don't need to be anywhere near the M25 to prosper. So our ears pricked up when we heard, recently, that the studio was taking on space in London. Und doch hat sich Studio Kiln im Jahr 2022 genau dort niedergelassen. Und seitdem läuft alles überraschend gut. Das Kreativbüro hat eine Reihe von Auszeichnungen gewonnen und sich einen guten Ruf für sein Branding und seine digitale Arbeit aufgebaut, beispielsweise für sein Partikelsystem für BAFTA. Das alles ist ein starker Beweis dafür, dass man nicht in der Nähe der M25 sein muss, um erfolgreich zu sein. Deshalb wurden wir hellhörig, als wir kürzlich hörten, dass das Studio Räumlichkeiten in London beziehen würde. Wir haben Nathan Smi getroffen

They are a brand of vacation homes called Leisurama, complete with a befittingly midcentury logo of bouncing letters. They were prefabricated and a few grand and came with Melmac plates, Murphy beds, and the postwar promises of summer fun and middle-class vacationing. items.summary_original: COOLING MOVES BACK INTO THE HOUSE At Jalmanjar Farmhouse outside Ahmedabad , cooling begins with a perforated facade of compressed earth blocks. This outer skin filters the sun while windcatchers draw air through the enclosure. items.title_de: Wie kann die Architektur ein Haus kühl halten, wenn der Strom ausfällt?
items.summary_de: Die Kühlung geht zurück ins Haus. Im Jalmanjar Farmhouse außerhalb von Ahmedabad beginnt die Kühlung mit einer perforierten Fassade aus komprimierten Erdblöcken. Diese Außenhaut filtert die Sonne, während Windfänger Luft durch das Gehäuse saugen. Dahinter befinden sich Veranden und Balkone, die den schattigen Raum zwischen dem Außenjali und den Innenräumen einnehmen, und ein offener Innenhof durchschneidet die Mitte des Grundrisses. Das Haus verfügt zwar über aktive Systeme, aber ein Großteil der thermischen Arbeit hat bereits in der Wand und im Hohlraum begonnen, bevor eine Maschine ins Spiel kommt. Bevor die Kühlung zu einem Gerät wurde, war sie ein integrierter Bestandteil des Gebäudes. Öffnungen waren den vorherrschenden Winden ausgesetzt, da die Luft einen Weg durch das Haus brauchte und Höfe kühlere Bereiche in der Nähe der bewohnten Räume bildeten. Dickes Mauerwerk verlangsamte den Wärmedurchgang

items.title: les caryatides de guyancourt: a photo essay on the postmodernist complex of suburban paris
items.summary_original: LES CARYATIDES DE GUYANCOURT BY Manuel Núñez Yanowsky Just southwest of Paris , at the intersection of Andrea Palladio and Frank Lloyd Wright streets in the suburb of Guyancourt, 18 colossal female figures stand together to support one of the most surreal manifestations of postmodernist architecture. Together, the monumental replicas of the Venus de Milo compose Les Caryatides, two identical apartment blocks standing across from each other, performing their own kind of concrete theater in full view of the public . The project was designed in 1992 by architect Manuel Núñez Yanowsky, who was one of the original team members of Ricardo Bofill's Taller de Arquitectura in early 1960s Barcelona, and went on to develop several important works, including the iconic Arènes de Picasso in Noisy-le-Gr

items.title: 'It simply fills my life and saves me': Inside Varya Yakovleva’s sketchbooks
items.summary_original: From a chance ink sketch to a full series of paintings and wooden sculptures, the illustrator and animator explains how Les Femmes sauvages came together. "I was playing with ink, and I linked a random sketch of a woman. I noticed her pose: she looked wild, like an animal," says Varya Yakovleva, describing the start of Les femmes sauvages, now a full series of paintings, drawings and wooden sculptures. "Something can be born out of change, out of experiment and surprise," she says. "Intuition tells you that this is something you need to develop, and then you begin to think. What can be drawn out of it, what it can be transformed into." Varya was born in Russia – "or more precisely, in the Soviet Union," she says – and trained for a decade across art college, institute and directing courses

items.title: Oficía Mono: Viel mehr als Typo fürs Büro
items.summary_original: Die Type- und Grafikdesignerin Charlotte Rohde sieht ihre Schriften oft als Personen. Das ist bei ihrem neusten Font nicht anders. Auf den ersten Blick ist Oficía Mono eine Monospaced Schrift, die (nicht nur aber auch) gut zu Büroanwendungen passt. Für Charlotte Rohde, die in den letzten drei Jahren als Gastprofessorin für Typografie und Type Design an der Bauhaus Universität Weimar unterrichtete, ist Oficía Mono aber viel mehr: Sie ist auch eine Büroangestellte, fasziniert von Finanzen, professionell, gleichzeitig aber auch mädchenhaft – was sich in den herzförmigen i-Punkten manifestiert. Charlotte Rohde beschreibt Oficía Mono als »Girl who is invested« , was meint sie damit? »Das ist ein Wortspiel, das mit dem Privaten und dem Beruflichen spielt. Ein Girl, dass invested ist, ist emotion

items.title: Fight for Kindness 2026 Campaign
items.summary_original: What can typography do beyond communicating words? Fight for Kindness 2026 explores how letters and visual messages can create connection, encourage empathy, and contribute to positive change. Initiated by TypeCampus and supported by Zetafonts Foundry , the project brings together designers from around the world who share one idea: using creativity to help shape a kinder and more inclusive society. Now in its fifth edition, Fight for Kindness has grown into a global creative movement. In 2026, more than 1,000 typographic messages from 83 countries and in 42 languages came together, reflecting a remarkable variety of cultures, perspectives, and visual traditions. items.summary_original: In organisations today, data has never been more available. Dashboards and performance decks exist for almost every function — sales, product, marketing, operations — and the tools to build them have never been more accessible. And yet, in weekly standups and quarterly reviews, the same thing happens constantly: someone shares the numbers, the room nods, and the meeting ends without a decision or clear direction .
